title: Claude Code reports tool outcomes by event, not exit code
body:
Read Claude Code outcomes from hook_event_name, gated on CLAUDECODE=1: PostToolUseFailure (error string, is_timeout) is a failure, PostToolUse with tool_response.interrupted === false is a success. Do not extend that reading to other hosts. Any hand registration of DD hooks for Claude Code must include PostToolUseFailure, as hooks/hooks.json does, or failures are never recorded.

Why: Recorded in a real session on 2026-09-24: a successful Bash call's PostToolUse carries {stdout, stderr, interrupted, isImage, noOutputExpected} and no exit code, and a failing call (exit 3) fired no PostToolUse at all. Before this, a full day of tests left 0 tool observations. Grok also sends PostToolUse, with an unverified shape.
not_derivable: A real session showed a failing Bash call fires no PostToolUse at all and a success carries no exit code; the code reads the events, nothing explains the absence.

evidence.summary: observationFromTool takes { claudeCode } and reads PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure only then.
PostToolUseFailure is registered to the observe command.
Stop asks after a failure read from the event, not from an exit code.
